title: Introduce proportional radius and chroma contrast guides for analytics widgets
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Analytics widgets (cards, small charts, legends, table rows) currently use hard-coded radius and shadow values that do not scale with density modes (compact vs comfortable) and create inconsistent visual weight across product surfaces. Color ramps are also drifting: low-contrast accent colors are causing legibility regressions in small label contexts.

Goal: Define a compact, proportional radius scale and a chroma-driven contrast guide for the token set that ensures consistent perceived elevation and legibility for embedded analytics. This ticket will produce token proposals, migration guidance, and a small Figma kit to validate visuals at multiple sizes and densities.
acceptance_criteria: Token proposal created: radius tokens (r-0..r-6) defined as proportional values relative to base spacing token
Chroma contrast guide documented with minimum contrast thresholds for primary/secondary/neutral accents across text sizes used in charts and legends
Figma kit with sample components (card, mini-chart, legend, table row) showing compact and comfortable modes delivered
Design sign-off from Product and Accessibility (a11y) with notes addressed
Migration doc and codemod spec for engineering to update existing components and theme overrides
design_decisions: Adopt proportional radii: use a 1:1.618 scaling factor seeded from base spacing (8px) so small radii feel related to gutters and controls
Introduce chroma contrast guide: define accent tokens with lab/chroma anchors rather than purely hex values to keep perceived saturation consistent across light/dark modes
Shadow elevation broken into three compact layers (ambient, penumbra, key) with tokenized alpha and y-offsets to permit subtle elevation on dense lists without increasing perceived heaviness
Keep existing semantic token names (e.g., surface-card, surface-elevated) but add density variants: surface-card.compact and surface-card.comfortable
tradeoffs: Pros: tighter visual coherence between spacing and corner radii; predictable scaling across breakpoints; improved chart label legibility
Cons: requires migration of many component styles and may cause minor visual churn on customer dashboards until rollout is completed
Mitigation: provide theme flags and a temporary 'legacy' token alias layer so customers can opt into the new tokens per route
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize token values and produce Figma kit; get PM + a11y review (this ticket)
Week 2: Create codemod spec and small migration PRs for card/table/chart components (ENG owners assigned)
Week 3: Release behind a feature flag (console-2026.04); visually QA high-traffic pages and dashboards; collect feedback
Week 4: Flip default for new projects; publish migration guide and deprecation timeline for legacy tokens
qa_checklist: Verify token aliasing: old token names map to new density-aware tokens via aliases
Visual validation on 3 sample apps: admin dashboard, customer report, embed preview
Color contrast checks for all text sizes in charts and legends using automated a11y tooling
Cross-browser spot check (Chrome, Safari, Edge) for shadow rendering differences
Performance sanity: confirm no large style recalculation spikes when applying new tokens
